## Overview

Natural Language Processing for Requirements Engineering (NLP4RE) is an area of research and development that seeks to apply natural language processing techniques, tools, and resources to the requirements engineering process, to support human analysts to carry out various linguistic analysis tasks on textual requirements documents, such as detecting language issues, identifying key domain concepts, and establishing requirements traceability links.

## Systematic Mapping Study Survey

A significant systematic mapping study was conducted on this topic. The systematic mapping study identified 404 relevant primary studies and reviewed them according to five research questions, cutting across five aspects of NLP4RE research, concerning the state of the literature, the state of empirical research, the research focus, the state of the practice, and the NLP technologies used. These 404 primary studies were published over the past 36 years and from 170 different venues, with most studies (67.08%) being solution proposals.

## Research Framework

The mapping study establishes a structure to frame the existing literature through categorization, synthesis and conceptualization of the main theoretical concepts and relationships that encompass both RE and NLP aspects, producing a conceptual framework of NLP4RE that is used to identify research gaps and directions, highlight technology transfer needs, and encourage more synergies between the RE community, the NLP one, and the software and systems practitioners.

## Workshop Series

The NLP4RE workshop serves as a regular meeting point for researchers on NLP technologies in RE.

## Overview
TAPHSIR decides for each pronoun occurrence in a requirements specification whether the pronoun is ambiguous or unambiguous, and further provides an automatic interpretation for the pronoun.

## Purpose and Functionality
TAPHSIR facilities reviewing the use of pronouns in a requirements specification and revising those pronouns that can lead to misunderstandings during the development process. TAPHSIR focuses on pronominal anaphoric ambiguity, an ambiguity type that has been explored only to a limited extent in requirements engineering.

## Overview

TAPHSIR was created by Saad Ezzini, Sallam Abualhaija, Chetan Arora, and Mehrdad Sabetzadeh in 2022, and was presented at the 30th ACM Joint European Software Engineering Conference and Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering (ESEC/FSE '22) in November 2022.

## Focus and Purpose

TAPHSIR focuses on pronominal anaphoric ambiguity, an ambiguity type that has been explored only to a limited extent in requirements engineering. The tool facilitates reviewing the use of pronouns in a requirements specification and revising those pronouns that can lead to misunderstandings during the development process by detecting requirements which have potential anaphoric ambiguity and attempting to interpret anaphora occurrences automatically.

## Technical Approach

TAPHSIR implements a hybrid solution where feature-based machine learning is used for detecting anaphoric ambiguity and a large-scale language model from the BERT family is used for anaphora resolution. The tool collects 45 language features that capture the characteristics of the relationship between the pronoun and its likely antecedent.
